alex: Morning handoff / postmortem note from the overnight window. We had a P1 at ~2026-06-12T23:42Z: routing-backpressure on hosted text-generation endpoints in ap-south (lots of 429s + client retries). Triggered by an accidental canary traffic leak to a degraded routing pool during a deployment. Pager fired, mitigations applied, and we transitioned to degraded (partial) by 00:30Z. No data loss.

emma: I picked up the pager and triaged. Timeline:
- 23:42Z pager: repeated 429s from region=ap-south
- 23:46Z identified spike coincident with canary rollout for ROUTER-1. Canary gate failed to keep traffic routed to healthy pool.
- 23:51Z enabled fallback-route and diverted canary traffic to standby pool.
- 00:05Z scaled routing pool +2 nodes, reduced max-concurrency on affected frontends.
- 00:30Z 429 rate down to baseline but p95 latency still elevated.

raj: I ran node checks and found increased queue_depth and backpressure metrics on router-3 and router-4. Logs show `accept loop` delays and repeated grpc backpressure events. Snippet from router-3: 

```bash
# check router queues
kubectl -n infra logs router-3 | grep queue_depth | tail -n 20
```

sample lines:
```
2026-06-12T23:45:59Z WARN router: queue_depth=265 high-water=200
2026-06-12T23:46:02Z ERROR router: backpressure: grpc_accept_delay=120ms
```

incident-bot: Pager: P1 - routing-backpressure - triggered by repeated 429s (region=ap-south). incident-id: INC-20260612-778. Acknowledged by emma at 23:47Z.

ops-runbook-bot: Runbook invoked: routing-fallback v1. Steps executed: toggle-fallback-route, scale-router-pool, throttle-canary. Docs: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/routing-fallback#v1

emma: Immediate mitigations we applied:
- Enabled `fallback-route` for ap-south to protect customer traffic.
- Set canary gate -> `off` temporarily to stop traffic leak.
- Throttled new connections on router frontends to prevent queue amplification.
- Created short-lived rate-limit override for critical customers to avoid asymmetric retries.

alex: Customer impact: several customers in APAC saw elevated 429s and repeated client retries for ~45 minutes. We escalated to support at 00:10Z and asked CS to notify a small set of affected accounts. No broad SLA breach expected but individual customers may need follow-up.

emma: Planned actions for our shift (next 8h):
- Keep canary disabled until post-mortem of routing rollout is complete.
- Run a controlled canary test in staging with traffic mirroring, then incrementally re-enable in prod with lower traffic-sample.
- Monitor router queue_depth and grpc_accept_delay on router-3..5 for sustained >120s or queue_depth>150 for >10m.
- If queue_depth persists, add +2 routers and trigger `force-drain` of router-3.

raj: Commands I used / recommend for followups: 

```bash
# drain router
./infractl router drain router-3 --timeout 600s --region ap-south
# scale routing pool
kubectl -n infra scale deployment/router --replicas=$(($(kubectl -n infra get deploy router -o=jsonpath='{.spec.replicas}')+2))
# quick check for grpc backpressure
kubectl -n infra logs router-3 | grep "grpc_accept_delay" | tail -n 30
```

emma: Support messaging suggestion (paste to #support-incidents):
"We experienced a partial outage for text-generation in APAC due to a routing canary leaking traffic to a degraded routing pool. Our engineers have rerouted traffic and applied mitigations; service is partially recovered. If you continue to see 429s, please provide request IDs and timestamps and we will prioritize those investigations. Expected full recovery after canary re-validation and controlled rollout (~2-5 hours)."

alex: Handoff assignments / coverage gaps: 
- Primary: emma (oncall) for the next 8 hours.
- Secondary: raj (pager backup).
- Alex: offline 14:00-17:00 UTC today for planned time off; reachable for critical emergencies via phone.
- If incident escalates to P0, escalate to platform-sre paging rotation and create an incident bridge.

emma: Action items for next shift (put in their handoff):
- Validate canary gating logic in deploy pipeline (PR: infra/ROUTER-guard).
- Run traffic-mirroring test and post results in #eng-oncall before re-enabling canary.
- Confirm customer follow-ups logged in INC-20260612-778.
- Add postmortem owner and tentative timeline for RCA (target draft in 48h).

raj: I'll keep the router dashboards up and will post health-check outputs every hour. If queue_depth >150 for 15m, I'll start the drain+scale steps and notify infra-sre.

emma: I'm taking primary. Ping me with @emma for anything urgent. :eyes:

alex: Thanks all. I'll add notes to the runbook about the canary gating failure and link the deploy CI logs: https://redwood.internal/ci/ROUTER-2026-06-12. Reference incident INC-20260612-778 for all follow-ups.

emma: Wrapping up handoff now. Leaving an abbreviated checklist in the incident runbook. File a postmortem if we don't have a clear single root cause after canary validation.
